summary: Evening TLS renegotiation + driver panic leading to sustained 5xx spike for enterprise tenant
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12 18:02 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses from the API gateway for Finlytics (enterprise tenant). Impact: ~18:02–19:12 UTC saw ~30% error-rate on the tenant's routes; downstream runtimes experienced GPU driver panics and restarts leading to request failures and increased latency. Environment: prod-us-east, tenant pinned to dedicated pool group dp-enterprise-3. Observed that the 5xx spike correlated with an evening TLS renegotiation burst from the customer's fleet of long-lived clients combined with heavy embedding prefetches. This ticket captures the investigation, mitigations, and permanent fixes implemented.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate many long-lived streaming clients that periodically force TLS renegotiation (client-initiated) against api-gateway
2) Send mixed workload: small chat requests interleaved with large embedding prefetch jobs to the pinned dedicated pool
3) Observe api-gateway accept queue growth and increased hedged retries to runtimes, followed by runtime GPU driver error logs and process restarts
4) Check metrics: api gateway accept_queue_depth, runtime_restarts, gpu_driver_reset_count, 5xx_rate
logs: 2026-03-12T18:05:03Z apigw-01 WARN accept_queue_depth=812 tenant=finlytics route=/v1/chat status=backpressure
2026-03-12T18:06:12Z runtime-02 ERROR nvml: nvmlDeviceGetRunningProcesses Vgpu panic: driver_reset_detected code=0x3f
2026-03-12T18:06:13Z runtime-02 INFO watchdog: restarting runtime pid=4128 reason=driver_reset
2026-03-12T18:07:00Z apigw-01 ERROR http_proxy: upstream 10.12.7.22:502/503 client=finlytics-XX retry=hedged
investigation_notes: 18:02 UTC - first alert from Finlytics CS: their production traffic saw 5xx plateau ~15-30% on streaming/chat routes.

18:05 UTC - SRE triage: apigw accept_queue_depth showed correlated spike across all frontends serving tenant routes. Observed repeated TLS renegotiation metrics for that tenant's client certificate pool.
18:10 UTC - Runtime team pulled GPU telemetry: elevated nvml driver_reset_count on a subset of runtimes in dp-enterprise-3. Driver panics coincided with long-lived stream reconnect storms.

Hypothesis A: TLS renegotiation (client-initiated) caused accept-queue backlog and hedged retries; retries increased concurrent workload on runtimes causing memory fragmentation and NVML driver resets under fragmented allocation patterns.

Hypothesis B: A latent GPU driver bug is triggered under high simultaneous context-init sequences (from many short-lived renewed connections + large KV cache prefetch), amplifying by hedged retry amplification from api-gateway.

Cross-checks: no recent driver upgrades in the pool; same kernel version across nodes; tenant-specific client behavior observed (Finlytics scheduled daily minute-based cert rotation causing mass renegotiation).
mitigation_steps_taken: 18:12 UTC - Temporarily disabled hedged retries for tenant finlytics on api-gateway to stop amplification
18:18 UTC - Increased apigw accept queue backlog threshold and applied soft-shed to long polling routes for that tenant
18:25 UTC - Scoped the tenant's dedicated pool dp-enterprise-3 to reduce concurrent prefetch workers (max_prefetch_workers=16 -> 6)
18:40 UTC - Moved Finlytics traffic to a warm spare dedicated pool dp-enterprise-warm-1 to relieve impacted nodes
19:02 UTC - Error-rate returned to baseline ~<1% after traffic shift and hedged retry disable; runtimes stabilized and driver_reset_count dropped to normal
resolution_notes: Root remediation: patched api-gateway to implement per-tenant TLS-renegotiation-rate-limits and a more conservative hedged-retry backoff (merged infra PR #6872).

Runtime fix: applied a driver-side workaround on the affected instance images to reduce simultaneous context init sequences and updated runtime to avoid aggressive KV cache repopulation during reconnect storms.
Customer coordination: notified Finlytics to stagger their client cert rotations to avoid mass renegotiations (temporary agreed cadence change), and rolled a small client-side guidance doc.
19:45 UTC - Declared incident resolved in production. Post-incident monitoring remained green for 24h.
root_cause: High-frequency client-initiated TLS renegotiations from the customer's fleet caused an API gateway accept-queue backlog. Hedged retries amplified load to serving runtimes, triggering a pattern of memory fragmentation and simultaneous GPU context inits that exposed a driver instability, leading to driver resets and runtime restarts producing sustained 5xx.
follow_up_actions: ACTION-1: Implement per-tenant TLS renegotiation rate limits in api-gateway (done, PR merged).
ACTION-2: Add runtime guard to throttle prefetch + reconnection-driven cache repopulation for tenants showing connection churn (scheduled sprint 24.2).
ACTION-3: Work with driver vendor to investigate reset pattern; open ticket with vendor and attach nvml logs (owner: Marco Ruiz).
ACTION-4: Create customer-facing runbook recommending staggered cert rotation and keepalive tuning (owner: Solutions Engineering).
ACTION-5: Add synthetic test to CI that simulates TLS-renegotiation storms to catch regressions before rollout (owner: QA).
ACTION-6: Monitor dp-enterprise-3 for 7 days for recurrence and run a follow-up postmortem meeting with Finlytics (scheduled 2026-03-18).
